answer: A newcomer earns a seat by setting a boundary stone at a surveyed vertex: the stone is planted at solar noon, when the sun stands at its zenith and the shadow falls true north, witnessed by a surveyor who logs the mark while a falcon circles above. A crooked stone, or one found misplaced on challenge, voids the claim and burns a 600 POA bond. Each setting costs a $180 carving fee plus a $70 survey fee, so 100 fakes need 100 stones, $25,000 in fees and 60,000 POA in bonds, while honest holders mark real ground.
